title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). L is an ordered set of 'moments' or 'lieux'. Grothendieck builds a set M = M0 ⊔ M1, where M0 = L and M1 = Drap_2(L), the 2-element chains {a<b}. Each chain gives an 'interval' I_{a,b} with support |I_{a,b}| = [a,b]; for a point, |a| = {a}. Two endpoint sets are attached: δI_{a,b} = ∂I_{a,b} = {a,b}, δx = {x}, ∂x = ∅. The relations already on M are:
- incidence X◁Y: X is an endpoint of the interval Y;
- containment X≪Y: |X| ⊂ |Y|;
- interior containment X∘≪Y: X = Y, or X is a point strictly inside Y, or X is a subinterval of Y.
He notes that ≪ is the disjoint union of ◁ and ∘≪ (with X = Y counted in ∘≪).

This page. The previous page closed with his own bracketed note that the order on M should have come first; this page does that and defines a strict order < on M:
- x<y when x<y in L;
- x < I_{a,b} when x ≤ a;
- I_{a,b} < y when b ≤ y;
- I_{a,b} < I_{a',b'} when b ≤ a'.
Equivalently, X<Y iff X≠Y and every element of δX is ≤ every element of δY. A margin note introduces the order on subsets: A≤B means every a∈A is ≤ every b∈B. Thus X<Y iff max δX ≤ min δY with X≠Y, i.e. X lies weakly to the left of Y, touching allowed only at a shared endpoint. In particular a < I_{a,b} < b, so M behaves like the cells of a subdivided line: points and the open intervals between them.

Notation. For a nonempty chain D, 'or D' (origin) is min D and 'ex D' (extremity) is max D. For X in M, or X = or δX and ex X = ex δX.

Remarks:
(a) X<Y implies ex X ≤ or Y.
(b) X ≤ Y implies or X < ex Y, unless X = Y is a single point.

Proposition. If X<Y, X'≪X and Y'≪Y, then X'<Y', or else X' = ex X = Y' = or Y.
Proof: ex X' ≤ ex X ≤ or Y ≤ or Y', and equality forces the degenerate case.

Corollary. In the degenerate case X' is an endpoint of X and Y' of Y, so they cannot be interior. Hence X<Y, X'∘≪X and Y'∘≪Y imply X'<Y'.

Definition. X|∘|Y iff X<Y or Y<X, i.e. {X,Y} is a 2-chain of (M,<); this is the comparability graph. With it he checks axioms 'Mag 3' and 'Mag 4' of some axiomatic structure. Mag 3 is plausibly stability of the relation under interior shrinking, which is exactly the Corollary. Mag 4 is plausibly that incidence implies the relation, since a < I_{ab} < b.

Purpose. The next page uses this to show that the 'parfigures' of M (the subsets that are 'figures') are exactly the chains of ≤. So the page is part of an axiomatic, combinatorial geometry of 'lieux/figures', modelled on the poset of points and intervals of an ordered set.
errors: The last line is written as 'X◁Y ⟺ X|·|Y'. Only ⟹ holds: two points x<y are comparable but not incident. Given the stated reason (a < I_ab < b), Mag 4 is presumably the implication. Alternatively the relation |·| (dot) differs from |∘| (circle) and is not defined on this page.

The proof sentence 'Dans ce dernier cas on aura X'◁X, Y'◁Y' is slightly loose. If X (resp. Y) is itself a point, then X' = X rather than X'◁X. The conclusion still holds: if both are points one gets X = Y, contradicting X<Y; if only one is a point, the other side gives a genuine endpoint, which is incompatible with ∘≪.
Remark (b) is stated for X ≤ Y with the exceptional case X = Y = a. It is fine, but under X<Y the exception never occurs.
The characterisation line at the top is labelled with an overwritten symbol. Mathematically it must read X<Y (strict), since it includes the condition X≠Y.

ideas.what: The poset M = L ⊔ Drap_2(L) of points and intervals of an ordered set, with the 'weakly-left-of' strict order (a < I_ab < b).
ideas.modern_name: Order on the cells of a subdivided chain; an interval-order variant / Allen's 'before or meets' relation for intervals including degenerate ones.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Interval orders: Fishburn (1970); interval relations: Allen (1983); cell posets of subdivided lines: standard combinatorial topology.

ideas.what: Stability of the order under shrinking to interior subcells (corollary X<Y, X'∘≪X, Y'∘≪Y ⇒ X'<Y'), used to verify axioms 'Mag 3' and 'Mag 4'.
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity of precedence under part-of; a mereotopological axiom (interior parthood vs. contact).

ideas.what: Comparability graph |∘| on M, used (next page) to characterise 'parfigures' as chains of ≤.
ideas.modern_name: Comparability graph; cliques of the comparability graph = chains.

missed.claim: The page encodes an axiomatic combinatorial 'geometry of lieux and figures' built from incidence (◁), containment (≪), interior containment (∘≪) and precedence (<). This is closely parallel to Allen's interval algebra and to mereotopology (contact vs. interior parthood), which the Grothendieck literature does not connect to his late 'Ateliers' notes. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.
missed.quote: Le corollaire précédent montre Mag 3, et Mag 4 immédiat, car a<I_{ab}<b
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for reconstructing what the 'Mag' axiom system in Grothendieck's 1986 notes is. It looks like a discrete, point-free axiomatics of space/time configurations, a theme otherwise studied in qualitative spatial reasoning. There is no new theorem here.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are elementary and correct order-theoretic verifications: a cell order on points and intervals, and monotonicity under interior containment. The only mildly interesting element is the unpublished axiomatic framework (the 'Mag' axioms, 'figures/parfigures') that it serves, which is not documented in the literature as far as I know.
transcription_corrections: The characterisation line should read 'X < Y ⟺ (X≠Y et (∀x∈δX, ∀y∈δY, x≤y)) ⟺ (|X|≠|Y| et |X|≤|Y|)'. The relation symbol is strict, and the ∨ at the end is a line-break mark or continuation, not a logical 'or'.
'Drap^*(L)' denotes nonempty flags (chains). 'or D' and 'ex D' are origin (min) and extremity (max).
Remark a) reads 'X < Y ⟹ (ex X ≤ or Y)', with the second clause 'et or X ≤ ex Y' struck out.
The final line is probably 'donc X◁Y ⟹ X|·|Y' (Mag 4). The relation symbol may be |·| or |∘|; the image is ambiguous.
The NB in the left margin reads roughly: 'Pour deux parties A,B d'un ensemble ordonné on introduit relations A≤B, A<B (A≤B ⟺ A=B ou A<B), i.e. permet une écriture plus explicite'.
